label: Formulated the foundational doctrine of Xing Shan (innate goodness of human nature)
description: Mencius (Mengzi) formulated and introduced the concept of "Innate Goodness of Human Nature (Xing Shan)", which became a seminal contribution in ethics philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in ethics.
historicalContext: Introduced during the Eastern & Axial Traditions as part of Mencius (Mengzi)'s canonical writings.

citations.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
citations.work: Innate Goodness of Human Nature (Xing Shan)

label: Engaged in Warring States dialectic over human nature, spontaneous instinct, and the artificiality of moral rituals
description: Zhuangzi (Chuang Tzu) engaged in a direct critique of Mencius (Mengzi)'s foundational principles, rejecting core axioms in favor of a dialectically opposed framework.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Mencius (Mengzi)'s perspective to Zhuangzi (Chuang Tzu)'s reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the Eastern & Axial Traditions era.
